evidence_summary: Positional cloning in breast/ovarian cancer families identified BRCA1 with germline mutations segregating with disease.
OlympiAD: olaparib prolonged progression-free survival versus standard therapy in germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer.
OlympiA: adjuvant olaparib improved invasive disease-free survival in germline BRCA1/2-mutated high-risk early breast cancer.
Identification of BRCA2 with germline mutations in breast cancer families.
OlympiAD enrolled germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 carriers; olaparib prolonged progression-free survival.
OlympiA enrolled germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 carriers; adjuvant olaparib improved invasive disease-free survival.
TOPARP-A: high response rate to olaparib among patients with DNA-repair defects including BRCA2.
PROfound: olaparib improved imaging-based progression-free survival in men with BRCA1/BRCA2/ATM alterations.
Germline DNA-repair mutations found in 11.8% of men with metastatic prostate cancer; BRCA2 most frequent.
Clinical sequencing of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer documented BRCA2 alterations among DNA-repair aberrations.
HER-2/neu amplification correlated with shorter time to relapse and overall survival in node-positive patients.
Adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy improved outcomes in HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer.
ASCO/CAP guideline defines HER2 testing to select patients for HER2-targeted therapy.
TCGA breast cancer project characterised the HER2-enriched subtype and ERBB2 amplification.
HERACLES: trastuzumab plus lapatinib was active in HER2-positive KRAS exon 2 wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer.
EBCTCG patient-level meta-analysis: tamoxifen substantially reduced recurrence in ER-positive disease; ER status was the main predictive factor.
ASCO/CAP guideline for ER/PR immunohistochemistry to identify candidates for endocrine therapy.
ASCO/CAP guideline recommends PR testing alongside ER.
EBCTCG meta-analysis: within ER-positive disease the benefit of tamoxifen did not depend materially on PR status.
Ki67 index distinguished luminal B from luminal A tumours with different recurrence and survival outcomes.
International working group recommendations highlight limited analytical standardisation of Ki67 despite prognostic associations.
SOLAR-1: alpelisib plus fulvestrant prolonged progression-free survival in PIK3CA-mutated HR-positive HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.
ESR1 ligand-binding-domain mutations found in hormone-resistant metastatic disease conferred ligand-independent ER activity.
Sequencing of metastatic tumours identified activating ESR1 mutations after endocrine therapy.
Review of TP53 mutations in human cancers including their prognostic associations.
TCGA documented frequent TP53 mutation particularly in basal-like tumours.
Analysis of 154 PALB2 mutation-carrier families estimated substantially increased breast cancer risk.
CHEK2 1100delC was enriched in familial breast cancer without BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations; estimated about two-fold risk increase.
The 21-gene recurrence score quantified distant-recurrence risk in tamoxifen-treated node-negative patients (NSABP B-14).
A gene-expression signature predicted short interval to distant metastases in young node-negative patients.
MINDACT: patients with high clinical but low genomic risk had high 5-year distant-metastasis-free survival without chemotherapy.
PAM50 subtype and risk-of-relapse score were prognostic in independent cohorts.
Gene-expression patterns defined intrinsic molecular subtypes of breast tumours.
TCGA analysis of invasive lobular carcinoma confirmed CDH1 loss as its hallmark alteration.
Somatic EGFR kinase-domain mutations were present in gefitinib-responsive non-small-cell lung cancers.
EGFR mutations correlated with clinical response to gefitinib.
IPASS: gefitinib superior to carboplatin-paclitaxel in EGFR-mutation-positive patients and inferior in mutation-negative patients.
FLAURA: osimertinib prolonged progression-free survival versus earlier EGFR inhibitors in untreated EGFR-mutated NSCLC.
TCGA lung adenocarcinoma profiling documented EGFR among recurrent driver alterations.
T790M was detected in tumours with acquired resistance to gefitinib or erlotinib and conferred resistance in vitro.
A second EGFR mutation (T790M) was identified at relapse on gefitinib and conferred drug resistance.
EML4-ALK fusion identified in NSCLC and shown to be transforming.
Crizotinib produced high response rates in ALK-rearranged NSCLC.
ROS1 rearrangements defined a distinct molecular subset of lung cancers sensitive to crizotinib in a case.
Crizotinib showed marked antitumour activity in ROS1-rearranged NSCLC.
Screening of lung cancers identified ROS1 fusions among other kinase fusions.
CodeBreaK 100: sotorasib produced durable responses in previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC.
Phase 1 trial: sotorasib showed anticancer activity in KRAS G12C-mutant solid tumours including NSCLC.
KRAS mutation was associated with absence of response to cetuximab.
CO.17: cetuximab benefit was confined to patients with KRAS wild-type tumours.
Panitumumab efficacy was confined to KRAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer.
PRIME: patients with RAS mutations did not benefit from panitumumab-FOLFOX4.
TCGA colorectal profiling documented frequent KRAS alterations.
PRIME extended RAS analysis: additional RAS (including NRAS) mutations predicted lack of panitumumab benefit.
BEACON CRC: encorafenib plus cetuximab (with or without binimetinib) improved overall survival in BRAF V600E-mutated colorectal cancer.
Dabrafenib showed antitumour activity in BRAF V600E-positive advanced NSCLC.
MET exon 14 splicing alterations were found across tumour types and associated with responses to MET inhibitors.
KIF5B-RET fusions identified in lung adenocarcinoma and shown to be oncogenic.
Screening of lung cancers identified RET fusions among kinase fusions.
LIBRETTO-001: selpercatinib produced durable responses in RET fusion-positive NSCLC.
KEYNOTE-024: pembrolizumab improved survival over chemotherapy in NSCLC with PD-L1 tumour proportion score of at least 50%.
Responses to anti-PD-L1 antibody were associated with PD-L1 expression in tumour-infiltrating immune cells across cancers.
Higher nonsynonymous mutation burden was associated with clinical benefit from pembrolizumab in NSCLC.
STK11/LKB1 alterations were associated with inferior response to PD-1 axis inhibitors in KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinoma.
Larotrectinib produced durable responses in TRK fusion-positive cancers across tumour types.
Larotrectinib produced durable responses in TRK fusion-positive cancers across tumour types (few colorectal cases).
Mismatch-repair-deficient colorectal cancers responded to pembrolizumab whereas proficient tumours did not.
Mismatch-repair deficiency predicted response to PD-1 blockade across 12 tumour types.
Somatic mutations at simple repeated sequences defined a subset of colorectal carcinomas.
TCGA identified a hypermutated colorectal subset largely associated with microsatellite instability.
Germline MLH1 mutations were identified in hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer kindreds.
An hMLH1 mutation was associated with hereditary non-polyposis colon cancer.
MSH2 cloned as a human mutator gene homologue and linked to hereditary non-polyposis colon cancer.
Germline MSH2 mutations were found in hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer kindreds.
Genes at the FAP locus on chromosome 5q21 were identified with mutations in affected patients.
ASCO tumour marker guideline supports serial CEA measurement for postoperative surveillance.
ASCO tumour marker guideline does not recommend CEA as a screening test for colorectal cancer.
PRESEPT: plasma methylated SEPT9 detected colorectal cancer in an asymptomatic screening population with limited sensitivity.
Multitarget stool DNA test had higher sensitivity than FIT for colorectal cancer but lower specificity.
Serum PSA was elevated in prostate adenocarcinoma and correlated with clinical stage.
Serum PSA measurement was evaluated as a screening test for prostate cancer.
PLCO: combined PSA and digital rectal examination screening did not reduce prostate cancer mortality over 7-10 years.
ERSPC: PSA-based screening reduced prostate cancer mortality but with substantial overdiagnosis.
Recurrent fusions of TMPRSS2 with ETS transcription factor genes (ERG; ETV1) identified in prostate cancer.
TCGA molecular taxonomy placed ERG fusions as the most frequent primary prostate cancer subclass.
DD3 (PCA3) identified as prostate-specific and highly overexpressed in prostate cancer.
Urinary DD3(PCA3) analysis was evaluated for prostate cancer diagnosis in men undergoing biopsy.
AR-V7 detection in circulating tumour cells was associated with resistance to enzalutamide and abiraterone.
AR gene amplification was found in tumours recurring during androgen-deprivation therapy.
Clinical sequencing of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer documented frequent AR alterations.
PTEN identified as a tumour suppressor mutated in prostate and other cancers.
Integrative genomic profiling of prostate cancer documented PTEN pathway alterations.
AMACR immunostaining distinguished prostate cancer from benign tissue.
Exome sequencing identified recurrent SPOP mutations defining a molecular subclass lacking ETS rearrangements.
TCGA molecular taxonomy included SPOP-mutant tumours as a subclass.
CDK12 biallelic loss defined a genomically distinct immunogenic class of advanced prostate cancer.
TOPARP-A responders included patients with ATM alterations.
PROfound cohort A combined BRCA1/BRCA2/ATM alterations; ATM-specific benefit is not separately curated here.
ATM was among germline DNA-repair genes mutated in men with metastatic prostate cancer.
AURA3: in T790M-positive advanced NSCLC that progressed on first-line EGFR inhibitor therapy, osimertinib prolonged progression-free survival compared with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy.

EMERALD: in ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer after CDK4/6-inhibitor therapy, elacestrant prolonged progression-free survival versus standard endocrine therapy, with greater benefit in tumours carrying ESR1 mutations.
